name: Mogodu
summary: Tripe stew: cleaned beef tripe simmered for hours until meltingly soft, then finished in a peppery onion, curry and tomato gravy and served with pap.
about: Mogodu (mala mogodu in Sesotho and Setswana, ulusu in isiXhosa and isiZulu) is one of South Africa's best-loved traditional dishes. It is cooked low and slow on weekends and for family gatherings, and eaten with stiff pap, dombolo or samp, often with chakalaka on the side.
steps: Rinse the tripe under cold running water, rubbing it between your hands, until the water runs clear and there is no grit left. Cut it into strips about 5 cm long.

Put the tripe in a large pot with the water, salt and bay leaves. Bring to the boil over high heat, skim off the grey foam that rises, then cover, lower the heat and simmer gently for 3 hours, topping up with boiling water to keep it covered, until a piece is soft when pinched.
Drain the tripe, keeping 2 cups of the cooking liquid, and set both aside.
Heat the oil in the same pot over medium heat and fry the onions and green pepper until soft and lightly golden, about 8 minutes.
Add the garlic, curry powder and paprika and stir for 1 minute until fragrant, then add the grated tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes until they thicken into a paste.

Return the tripe to the pot with the stock cubes, black pepper and the reserved cooking liquid. Stir, cover and simmer over low heat for 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until the gravy has thickened and coats the tripe.
Taste and add more salt or pepper if needed, scatter over the parsley and serve hot with stiff pap or dombolo.
prepNote: Boil the tripe until tender a day ahead and refrigerate it in its liquid; finish the gravy on the day.
